items.q: What distinguishes diuretic-resistant ascites from diuretic-intractable ascites in patients with chronic liver disease?
opts: Resistant fails to respond to full doses; intractable cannot tolerate full doses due to complications
Resistant is caused by portal vein thrombosis; intractable is caused by hepatic vein thrombosis
Resistant responds only to loop diuretics; intractable responds only to aldosterone antagonists
Resistant has high SAAG with low protein; intractable has low SAAG with high protein
items.exp: Diuretic-resistant ascites shows no response to full-dose diuretics, whereas diuretic-intractable ascites cannot receive full-dose diuretics due to development of diuretic-induced complications. (Book p1008)

items.q: Diuretic-resistant ascites is characterized by lack of response to full-dose diuretics, defined in the notes as spironolactone (printed as 40 mg / intended full dose 400 mg) combined with furosemide (Lasix) ________.
items.exp: In diuretic-resistant ascites, there is no response to full-dose diuretics: spironolactone (printed as 40 mg, full dose 400 mg) plus 160 mg lasix. (Book p1008)

items.q: Untreated or worsening diuretic-resistant ascites typically progresses directly to which life-threatening complication?
items.exp: Diuretic resistant ascites is noted as: 'Progresses to HRS'. (Book p1008)

items.q: Match each subtype of refractory ascites with its clinical definition and features: 1. Diuretic Resistant Ascites 2. Diuretic Intractable Ascites
opts: 1: Lack of response to full doses (Lasix 160 mg + spironolactone), progresses to HRS; 2: Inability to tolerate full doses due to complications like hypo/hyperkalemia or renal failure
1: Inability to tolerate full doses due to complications like hypo/hyperkalemia or renal failure; 2: Lack of response to full doses (Lasix 160 mg + spironolactone), progresses to HRS
1: Responsive only to salt restriction alone without medications; 2: Complete resolution following a single diagnostic paracentesis
1: Caused by bacterial translocation into the ascitic space; 2: Caused by lymphatic rupture into the peritoneal space
items.exp: Diuretic resistant ascites is defined by failure to respond to full-dose diuretics and progresses to HRS; diuretic intractable ascites is defined by inability to titrate to full dose due to complications such as electrolyte imbalance (hypo/hyperkalemia) or renal failure. (Book p1008)

items.q: Diuretic-intractable ascites occurs when full diuretic doses cannot be administered due to medical complications. Which of the following is NOT an example of such a diuretic complication?
items.exp: Examples given for diuretic-intractable ascites complications are hypokalemia, hyperkalemia, and renal failure. (Book p1008)

items.q: What definitive interventional radiological procedure is indicated for the management of refractory ascites?
items.exp: Under refractory ascites, the designated management is TIPSS (Transjugular Intrahepatic Portosystemic Shunt). (Book p1008)
